Fetch a Switzerland-wide boundary layer from the BFS

pv_fetch_map.Rd

Downloads the map layers too large to bundle with the package. pv_fetch_map("municipalities") returns the boundary polygons of all Swiss municipalities (status 1 January 2025) as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection stored as a plain R list — the same layout as pv_swiss_cantons — with each feature carrying id (the official BFS municipality number) and name. pv_choropleth() and pv_bubble_map() call this for you when given map = "municipalities".

Usage

pv_fetch_map(layer = "municipalities", refresh = FALSE)

Arguments

layer

The layer to fetch. Currently "municipalities" — the canton, district, and lake layers are bundled as pv_swiss_cantons, pv_swiss_districts, and pv_swiss_lakes and need no fetching.

refresh

Set to TRUE to bypass the cache, download the asset again, and rebuild the processed layer.

Value

A GeoJSON FeatureCollection stored as a plain R list, ready for the map argument of pv_choropleth() and pv_bubble_map(); source and licence are attached as attributes and printed on every fetch.

Details

The first call downloads the BFS "Generalisierte Gemeindegrenzen" (GG25) asset and needs the sf package to reproject it from the Swiss LV95 grid to the WGS84 longitude/latitude D3 expects; the processed layer is then kept in the polyviz download cache (see pv_cache_status()), so later calls are instant, work offline, and no longer need sf.

The Bundesamt für Statistik publishes these boundaries for open use with source citation required ("© BFS, ThemaKart"); every fetch prints these terms and attaches them to the result (pv_source, pv_licence, pv_url).

See also

pv_swiss_cantons, pv_cache_status()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
muni <- pv_fetch_map("municipalities")
length(muni$features)
} # }
